h: Shabbos Joy Reveals the Light Before Rosh Hashanah

p: שֶׁכׇּל שַׁבָּת יֵשׁ לוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת
that every Shabbos has a particular holiness
"the olah of each Shabbos on its Shabbos";
and in the parshah that is read on that Shabbos,
the aspect of the holiness particular
And in this parshah it is written:
"You are standing today, all of you,
that is, each and every one of Yisrael
merits to point with the finger,
as at the splitting of the Sea,
where each one said, "This is my God"
And of this we say "His light,"
that is, the light of Torah,
which is the holiness from the words of Torah
And the haftarah of this Shabbos,
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת זֶה
which is also the holiness of this Shabbos,
and this is the consolation from the side of Yisrael,
and says, "I will greatly rejoice," etc.
"For with joy you will go out," etc.;
"I said, the world will be built with kindness":
חֶסֶ״ד סָלִיק לְחוּשְׁבַּן ע״ב שְׁמָהָן וְכוּלֵּי
"chesed adds up to the number of the seventy-two Names," etc.;
"and this is the morning of Avraham," etc.;
"'and a throne will be established through kindness,'" etc.;
'As in the days of your going out of the land of Egypt
and the secret of the redemption
'For with joy you will go out,'" etc.;
for it corresponds to the middah of Kesser Elyon,
which is entirely hidden from all conception,
And the beginning of the revelation
is the utterance "Let there be light,"
and it corresponds to the letter yud,
which is the aspect of thought,
and its crown alludes to Kesser Elyon,
And this is the aspect of the first light,
which was hidden away for the righteous.
And this is why we say,
to which the Tikkunei Zohar alludes:
and placed it for them in its place,
and the rest He hid away for the righteous," etc.
And on Shabbos, in which there is
a little revelation of the first light,
it is in the aspect of "For with joy you will go out";
for when one merits the revelation of the first light,
that it shines in the heart
one consequently merits to straighten the heart;
"and for the upright of heart, gladness";
and at the end (of the first chapter of Taanis, Taanis 15a):
And this is what it says (Sifrei, Beha'alosecha):
"'And on the day of your rejoicing' (Bamidbar 10:10):
שֶׁאַף שֶׁלֹּא נִצְטַוּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת עַל שִׂמְחָה
for although there was no command of rejoicing on Shabbos,
And this is what it says:
"For with joy you will go out":
besimchah has the letters of machashavah,
and the revelation of the first light
that the seven haftaros of consolation
from above to below and from below to above.
corresponds to the middah of Chesed,
the secret of the seventy-two Names.
וְחֶסֶד עִלָּאָה נָפְקָא מֵחָכְמָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קעה, ב)
And "upper Chesed issues from Chochmah" (Zohar II 175b).
this haftarah corresponds to the middah of Malchus.
And both are preparation for Rosh Hashanah,
And this is why we say on the preceding Shabbos,
And likewise the middah of Malchus,
"Say before Me on Rosh Hashanah," etc.,
so that you make Me King over you";
and as the Men of the Great Assembly instituted
in the Tefillah of Rosh Hashanah:
"And You will reign, You, Hashem our God,
